translated_text: December 12, 1938. My dearest, I received your letter of the 9th today. Oh, it really seems we're making progress! I'm still not entirely sure whether I should go to the consulate before I can get a new passport. I have to wait for my father's message about that. I might briefly and superficially inquire about the duplication. I don't want to give the impression of being pushy if I can come later with the new passport. I've inquired about joining a journalists' association. It's very difficult, though, as this profession requires a business license, which you have to present. Whether I'll succeed is still uncertain. I know someone who could help me with that, but I'd like to avoid it if possible. I've told you about it. It would be good if you wrote me a letter about it. It certainly won't be long now, my dear. Everything will be so beautiful, and I even believe we've earned this beauty through hard work and honesty. Then whatever happens in the world can happen. Things will be so much easier together. All our worries will be only half as heavy. At least we'll have someone we can confide in – soon, soon! – Your mom came back from Budapest yesterday. She's so happy to be home again. Unfortunately, there's no hope left for Grandma, but I'm thinking of making positive preparations for emigration while I'm in Paris. Listen to this sometime. More about that soon. Your Zot.
